rule: Generic/template type arguments are dropped from every ID (`HashSet#<init>`). | a receiver whose type is given by a declaration — local, parameter, field/property (including `$var->prop` / `obj.field` chains whose property has a declared type), catch parameter, for-loop variable, pattern binding — or by `= new T(...)` gives `T#m` (high if defined in the scan, else medium). | A pointer, reference or smart pointer whose `->`/`.` reaches the pointee names the pointee | **medium**: the callee is named statically (Type.m(), module.f(), an import, `self.m()` inherited from a base outside the scan, an external library type) but is not defined in the scan.
source: KNOWN_GAP: methods of some generic-instance types are misnamed at medium
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a free function (`file.f`, `std.x.f`) is `direct`. All files sit directly under src/, so the file qualifier is the basename (`app`, `util`). Receivers declared with an instantiated generic std type: field `ids` reached through `self.ids` (an `obj.field` chain whose property has a declared type), pointer parameter `*std.AutoHashMap(u32, u32)` (names the pointee), value parameter. Type arguments are dropped → `std.AutoHashMap#m`, medium. Any other name for these (e.g. carrying `(u32, u32)`, or the std implementation type `HashMap`/`HashMapUnmanaged`, which the scan cannot see) is wrong.
